title: Buddy ECC: Making Cache Mostly Clean in CXL-Based Memory Systems for Enhanced Error Correction at Low Cost
problem: CXL Memory Modules have different characteristics than traditional DRAM DIMMs, making existing cache and reliability optimizations ineffective; there is a need to optimize bandwidth, enhance reliability, and reduce area overhead for CXL systems.
motivation: CXL is emerging as a key memory interconnect standard, but its full-duplex nature and features are not fully exploited by current optimization techniques.
method: The approach uses three techniques that work together. First, it predicts when data blocks will no longer be accessed and proactively writes them back to main memory, reducing the number of dirty cachelines (modified data still in cache). Second, it monitors the CXL Memory Module's bandwidth usage and only performs these write-backs during idle periods to avoid slowing down other traffic. Third, Buddy ECC assigns different levels of protection: stronger error correction (ECC, which detects and fixes errors) for the remaining dirty cachelines, and simpler error detection (EDC, which detects but doesn't fix errors) for clean cachelines, since they're safely backed up in main memory.
key_novelty: Buddy ECC exploits CXL's full-duplex capabilities (simultaneous two-way data transfer) to dynamically adjust error-protection strength based on cacheline state, using strong ECC for dirty cachelines and weak EDC for clean ones.
contributions: Energy consumption increase under 1% while enhancing reliability
limitations: Limitations not discussed; scalability to heterogeneous memory hierarchies unclear.
primary_theme: CXL memory optimization with adaptive error correction
